title: totalPaid return value reports 0 when caller actually spent paymentAmount and received an unrelated donation refund as a windfall
description: When a third-party donation pre-loads the BatchNFTMinter contract balance, `remaining > paymentAmount` after the loop. The clamp `paymentAmount > remaining ? paymentAmount - remaining : 0` returns `totalPaid = 0` even though the dispatcher pulled real cost. Off-chain accounting that trusts the return value treats a paid mint as free.
impact: No on-chain asset loss. The caller's wallet flow is internally consistent: paid the dispatcher the real cost, received a donor-funded refund as a windfall, net wallet position correct. Only the helper's `totalPaid` return value is wrong — an off-chain accounting / integrator gotcha for any consumer that records the call cost from the return value.
attackPath: Third party donates D wei of paymentToken to BatchNFTMinter (windfall, no malicious intent required)
Caller invokes batchMint(paymentAmount=P) which costs C < P + D
Loop completes; remaining = P + D - C
Sweep transfers (P + D - C) back to caller; clamp returns totalPaid = P > remaining ? P - remaining : 0
If P + D - C > P (i.e. D > C), totalPaid = 0 even though the dispatcher charged C of real cost
Off-chain integrator records the mint as zero-cost
recommendation: Either snapshot the pre-call contract balance and compute `totalPaid = paymentAmount + preBal > remaining ? paymentAmount + preBal - remaining : 0` (so the return value reflects the actual contract balance delta), OR document in NatSpec that `totalPaid == 0` does not imply zero-cost mint when donations are present so integrators do not mis-account.
severityRationale: CONFIRM low. Off-chain accounting gotcha with no on-chain asset risk. Either snapshot pre-call balance (computing totalPaid against the actual contract delta) or document the asymmetry in NatSpec. QA report.

classification.assetImpact: No on-chain asset loss. The caller's wallet flow is internally consistent: paid the dispatcher the real cost, received a donor-funded refund as a windfall, net wallet position correct. Only the helper's totalPaid return value is wrong — an off-chain accounting/integrator gotcha.
classification.likelihood: Low. Requires a non-trivial donation. Documented donation-flow-forward behavior makes this a corner case rather than a likely production scenario.
classification.assumptions: Donations occur (per NatSpec, this is acknowledged as possible).
classification.externalRequirements: Off-chain consumer that trusts the totalPaid return value.

scannerAttribution.dedupNotes: Adjacent to ECON-008 (donor-windfall MEV race) but different root cause: ECON-008 is about who captures the donation; DEDUP-007 is about the return value being wrong for the user who legitimately paid. Kept separately because the mitigations differ (snapshot pre-balance vs restrict refund recipient).

sanitization.notes: Not a known issue (BatchNFTMinter natspec acknowledges donation flow-forward but does not address the totalPaid-return-value asymmetry). Not in prior submissions. Distinct from prior-audit nft-staking-07 L-01 (NFTStaker donation grief on _recomputeSchedule) — different contract, different mechanism (return value vs schedule perturbation).
